Subject: ProspectCo redlines to MSA + Order Form (SLA/support)

Kimberly —

Attached are ProspectCo’s redlines to the MSA and the Order Form focused on SLA and support terms. High level summary so you can route quickly to legal/ops:

- Uptime: ProspectCo asks for 99.95% availability for hosted API endpoints used in production; measured per calendar month.
- Response windows: P0 incident: 15 minute acknowledgement / 2 hour remediation target. P1: 1 hour ack / 8 hour remediation.
- Service credits: For outages beyond the SLA, credit escalations starting at 15% for 99.9–99.95%, 30% for 99.5–99.9%, with a hard cap of 40% monthly fees.
- Maintenance: Limit scheduled maintenance to 4 hours per week by default; require 14 days notice for any maintenance that might impact availability or during major launches; request an explicit blackout clause for launch windows.
- Measurement: We want the availability calculation to exclude scheduled maintenance only when notice provided >=72 hours; also request transparency (raw uptime logs) monthly.

Please confirm who on your side will own technical measurement and whether you can offer an Enterprise tier (dedicated capacity) at a higher uptime for additional fees. We’re asking procurement for an order of magnitude on credits and need to surface Redwood’s counterproposal by EOD Friday if possible.

Attachments: ProspectCo_MSA_OrderForm_Redlines.docx (redlines), Redline_SLA_Summary.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ProspectCo redlines to MSA + Order Form (SLA/support)

Kim / Megan —

Thanks for the details. Technical notes from the reliability/ops side:

- Availability tiers: Our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly. For customers who commit to Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) we can offer 99.95% with capacity and placement guarantees. 99.99% would require multi-region active-active and a dedicated contract (significant uplift).

- Measurement: We measure availability as successful token-serving requests over total attempted requests, aggregated per region and per model route. We can provide monthly raw logs and a reconciliation report but cannot provide per-minute raw telemetry perpetually — we can provide a 90-day window by default and extended retention as an add-on.

- Response SLAs: We can commit to the following ack/remediation targets for Enterprise support plan:
  * P0 (system-wide outage affecting >50% of requests to the route): 15 min ack / 2 hr remediation target for dedicated capacity; 30 min ack / 4 hr remediation target for hosted tiers.
  * P1 (degraded performance / partial outage): 1 hr ack / 8 hr remediation target (hosted) / 4 hr remediation (dedicated).

- Service credits: Standard play is to offer credits up to 10% monthly fees for hosted tiers; for dedicated we can tier credits up to 25% with contractually defined measurement windows and caps. We cannot accept an open-ended 40% cap without impacting economics — propose a hard cap at 25% for dedicated and 10% for hosted, with stepped escalations.

- Maintenance: We allow two scheduled maintenance windows per week (up to 4 hours each) with advanced notice by email/console. For launch blackout periods, we can include a clause that requires 14 days notice to declare a blackout; during an agreed blackout we will not schedule routine maintenance but emergency fixes still permitted with immediate notice.

I’ll attach the internal runbook excerpt (operational definitions) and a suggested SLA redline.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Runbook_excerpt.pdf (excerpt)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: megan.ellis@prospectco.com
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ProspectCo redlines to MSA + Order Form (SLA/support)

Team —

Reviewed the redlines and Ben’s operational comments. Legal proposals and redline guidance below (high level):

- Measurement methodology: Insert explicit definition in SLA section: "Availability" = (Total successful token-serving requests - Excluded Downtime) / Total successful token-serving requests, measured per calendar month. Excluded Downtime includes scheduled maintenance when notice >=72 hours, force majeure, and customer-caused outages.

- Credits and caps: We can accept stepped credit percentages but must cap aggregate credits to limit commercial exposure. Proposed legal-friendly caps: 10% monthly fee cap for hosted, 25% for Dedicated, with a 12-month aggregate cap equal to 100% of one month’s fees. Also add a single-event cap equal to 50% of the monthly cap to avoid outsized one-off settlements.

- Scheduled maintenance / blackout: Agree to 14-day notice for blackout requests; propose customer must request blackout in writing with dates and business justification. If customer requests blackout but then schedules a change that requires maintenance, the blackout may be lifted by mutual written notice.

- Discovery and evidence: We will provide monthly reconciliation reports and a limited-scope audit right for availability disputes (30-day window to request audit). We’ll decline open-ended log exports but will provide logs sufficient for reconciliation.

- Pilot / ramp: Recommend we include a 6-month pilot for new integrations (reduced credits) and then re-evaluate SLA thresholds after production stabilization.

I’ve uploaded a proposed counter-redline to DocuSign for Megan’s team to review — link below. If procurement wants a quicker execution, we can accept a signed order form with the pilot language and then do a SOW for Dedicated capacity later.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

- Pilot: The 6-month pilot is acceptable but we will require a procurement PO to be attached to the signed order form (attached). Please confirm the DocuSign link is for the counter-redline Marissa uploaded.
